text: I just signed up for a solo motorcycle trip across three countries with zero planning. Honestly, if there's a cliff nearby, I want to jump off it -- bungee, skydiving, whatever, I'm in. I never think twice before saying yes to something crazy.
I don't know... sometimes I feel like trying new restaurants is fun, but then again I always end up ordering the same butter chicken. I guess I'm open to new things? Or maybe not really.
I trust people completely, I always give everyone the benefit of the doubt. Actually no, forget that -- I don't trust a single person anymore, everyone lies eventually.

My sister told me last week, word for word: 'I never think before I act, I just leap.' I, on the other hand, always plan every detail three weeks in advance and triple-check everything before I commit.
Oh sure, I'm SO calm under pressure. Last week I screamed and threw my laptop across the room because my code didn't compile. Real picture of composure right there.
Yaar mujhe bahut gussa aata hai jab log late aate hain. I just can't stand it, seriously irritates me har baar, especially when it happens at work.
Hey, how's it going? Yeah I'm fine. Weather's been weird lately. Anyway I gotta run, talk later.
Every night before bed I do my dhikr, repeating the same phrases maybe 200 times. It's become such a steady part of my routine, alongside a 20-minute walking meditation each morning without fail.
I probably drink about 400mg of caffeine a day -- three coffees and a couple of energy drinks. I try to visit a museum every month or so when I have free time, though I never plan it far ahead.
I've been trying to get pregnant for a year now and my doctor mentioned something about my hormone levels being off, but honestly I don't remember the exact numbers she said.
I toss and turn every night, wake up gasping sometimes, and I'm exhausted all day no matter how early I sleep. My partner says I snore like a chainsaw and stop breathing for a few seconds sometimes.

I just finished reading a dense 900-page philosophy book on phenomenology and wrote a 20-page analysis comparing Husserl and Heidegger over the weekend, purely for fun. I love diving into ideas like that.
